title.suggested: Mrs. Hartgrove may not get Tom Allen's estate

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic reported that Allen's widow in Birmingham, England, may claim his small estate instead of Tillie Hartgrove, his heir. Daughter Polly Taylor said her parents never divorced.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'The Republic: Wednesday, July 29, 1903', page 8.

facts.fact: Allen's estate, willed to Tillie Hartgrove, was worth less than $300 in personal effects and might go instead to his widow in Birmingham, England
Allen's daughter Mrs. Polly Taylor told the public administrator that her mother was living and had never been divorced from Allen
Allen's will left $10 each to his daughters Mrs. Taylor of St. Louis and Mrs. J. H. Newey of Birmingham, England, and did not mention his wife
Attorney Simon Bass, named executor, declined to act, and Public Administrator Garrard Strode took charge of the estate and filed its inventory in probate
The inventory listed the old concert piano from Allen's saloon on Market near Seventh Street, a champion's cup, a horse and harness, a barrel of whisky, furniture and pictures
places: Market Street near Seventh Street, St. Louis

facts.fact: Tillie Hartgrove, who nursed Allen in his last illness and was to marry him, paid the undertaker in advance for his funeral
